summary: Port nails the rainbow staircase's geometry, hue mapping and ramp slope exactly, but runs 1.33x too fast, sits ~47% too bright (its tallest column overflows the grid and saturates at the base), and — the big one — parks the bouncing ball ~10 rows too low so it spends about half of every cycle off the bottom edge instead of arcing brightly over the stairs.
observations: Rig: 16x16 grid, 256 px, no controls on either side (probe.json: 'no settable controls' for orig and port). Both sides compile and run clean, no runtime errors, seed-independent (seed 1 vs 1234 give identical stats), sensors not bound.

Shared structure (correct on both sides): a 4-step staircase, each step exactly 4 columns wide, tallest at the left, descending left-to-right; step-to-step height difference measured at 3.74 rows on BOTH sides (orig bar tops at rows 3.65/7.41/11.12/14.88 at t=0; port 2.12/5.82/9.59/13.35 — diffs 3.70-3.77 on both).

Shared colour law (exact match): hue is a pure function of column index, 24 deg per column (hue = col/15 of the wheel). Measured from the t=0 bottom row on both sides: col0 0deg, col1 24, col2 48, col3 72, col4 96, col5 120, col6 144, col7 168, col8 192(.7), col9 216, col10 240, col11 264. Identical to within rounding.

Shared vertical ramp slope (exact match): within a column, brightness steps by exactly 17 counts per row on both sides (= 255/15), rising toward the bottom of the grid; the ramp scrolls upward and wraps by one stair step.

SPEED: the port's animation cycle is 1.33x too fast. Measured from the col-0 sawtooth reset times: orig period 1.305 s (resets at 1.30/2.60/3.90/5.20/6.60/7.90/9.20/10.50 s), port 0.980 s (1.00/2.00/2.90/3.90/4.90/5.90/6.90/7.90 s). Ratio 1.332.

Both sides are FPS-INVARIANT (time-based, not frame-stepped): the same periods come out at 10, 20 and 40 fps (orig 1.300/1.313/1.308 s; port 0.980/0.982/0.980 s). So the speed gap is a real rate error, not frame coupling.

BRIGHTNESS: port mean brightness 32.3 vs orig 21.9 (+47%), stable across every window tested (6 s, 30 s, 60 s, 240 s, and a --skip 120 late window). Both sides brightnessTrend 'steady', zeroMotionFrames 0-1.

Cause of the brightness gap: the port's stair ramp is offset ~25 counts (~1.5 rows) higher than the original's at every phase. Orig col-0 bottom-row value cycles over [191, 254] and the top 1-2 rows of the grid stay black; port cycles over [216, 283-clipped-to-255], fills all 16 rows, and its bottom 1-2 pixels SATURATE at 255 for ~0.4 s of every 0.98 s cycle (~40% duty). Example t=0.9 col0 top-to-bottom: orig 0,0,16,33,...,220,237 (row0 dark, peak 237); port 23,40,57,...,244,255,255 (row0 lit, base railed).

SATURATION: at equal brightness the port's pixels are about half as saturated. Both sides follow (1-s) = v/256 - c with identical slope, but c = 0.257 on the original vs 0.106 on the port. Concretely, orig's peak red base pixel is (252,126,126) (s=0.50) where the port's is (255,191,191) (s=0.25) — the port's stairs read visibly washed-out/pastel at the base.

THE BALL — the headline divergence. Original: a soft ~4x4 px cyan blob centred exactly on column 7.5 (x centroid 7.50-7.61 in every one of 121 dumped frames, no horizontal motion), bouncing VERTICALLY in the upper half of the grid. Its y centroid oscillates 2.21 <-> 7.03 (rows 1..8 of 16) sinusoidally with period 1.305 s, peak pixel value a steady 168-187, total residual energy 880-948 every single frame — it is never absent and always sits against black, well clear of the staircase.

Port's ball: same column (x 7.5-8.0), same size and same peak brightness, but its y centroid oscillates 11.55 <-> off-grid. It is only visible rows ~11.5-15; extrapolating its speed (max 18 rows/s) the sinusoid is centred near row 14.4 with amplitude ~2.9, i.e. it dives to about row 17 — 2 rows BELOW the bottom of the grid. In the 121-frame dump the port's ball is completely absent from the render in 5 of every 10 frames (e.g. t=0.5-0.8, 1.5-1.9, 2.5-2.8), and when present it is buried inside the bright staircase rather than silhouetted against black. Residual energy 144-430 vs the original's steady ~900.

Ball size and shape are NOT the problem: on a 32x32 re-render the original's ball at t=0 spans cols 12-19 / rows 7-14 with peak 219, the port's spans cols ~13-18 / rows 26-30 with peak 210 — same soft radial kernel, same peak, just ~10 rows (2/3 of the grid height) lower.
Ball period tracks its own side's staircase: orig ball apexes every 1.30 s, port's every ~1.0 s — so the 1.33x speed error is global, not a separate ball bug.

RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE: both sides are resolution-independent and agree on that. Re-rendered at 8x8 and 32x32 the picture is the same, just coarser/finer (orig mean 23/21.9/21, port 34/32.3/31 at 8x8/16x16/32x32), and normalized feature positions carry over (orig ball centre 5.17/15 = 0.34 at 16x16 vs 11/31 = 0.35 at 32x32; port 0.91 vs 0.90).

NO REGIMES: a 240 s / 2 fps survey shows a completely uniform rhythm image on both sides — no mode rotation, no slow palette walk, no drift. meanBrightness min/max over 480 frames is 20-23 (orig) and 31-34 (port). Steady state at t=120-126 s is identical to t=0-6 s on both sides.

Visible signature difference in the whole-window rhythm images: the original shows a distinct bright teal stripe at ~47% of the width (the ball's column-mean contribution at cols 7-8); on the port that stripe is faint and intermittent.
feedback: Slow the whole animation down by a factor of 1.332: the port's master cycle is 0.980 s where the original's is 1.305 s. Both the stair scroll and the ball bounce share that one rate, so a single speed constant fixes both. Verify by the col-0 sawtooth reset spacing (should be 1.30 s at any fps).

Move the bouncing ball up by about 10 rows (0.65 of the grid height). Target: on a 16-row grid the ball's centre should oscillate between row 2.2 and row 7.0 (normalized y 0.15 to 0.47) — i.e. entirely in the TOP half, above the staircase, against black. The port currently oscillates around row ~14.4 with amplitude ~2.9 rows, so it clips through the bottom edge and is completely off-screen for about half of every cycle. This is the pattern's most visible element and right now a viewer barely sees it.

Reduce the ball's oscillation amplitude slightly once it is repositioned: original peak-to-peak centroid travel is 4.8 rows (amplitude ~2.4 rows on a 16-row grid); the port's fitted amplitude is ~2.9 rows.

Everything else about the ball is already correct — keep it: column 7.5 with no horizontal motion, ~4 px soft radial kernel, peak value ~180-220, sinusoidal (not gravity-arc) easing, and the same period as the staircase.

Lower the stair ramp's overall offset by ~25 counts (~1.5 rows). The original's tallest column peaks at a bottom-row value of 252-254 and never saturates, leaving the top 1-2 rows of the grid black at all times; the port reaches an effective 283, so it fills the full column height and rails its bottom 1-2 pixels at 255 for ~40% of each cycle. Fixing this offset should bring mean brightness from 32 down to the original's 22.

The same offset fix should also correct the saturation: at the same brightness the port is about half as saturated as the original (orig peak base pixel (252,126,126), port (255,191,191)). Both sides use the same (1-s) vs v slope, so this is one shared offset error, not a separate colour bug — but re-check it after the brightness fix rather than tuning saturation separately.

Do NOT touch: the hue-per-column mapping (24 deg/column, verified exact for cols 0-12), the 17-counts-per-row ramp slope, the 4x4-column stair layout, the 3.74-row step height, the upward scroll direction and sawtooth wrap, resolution independence, or fps-invariance — all of these already match the original exactly.
